source.title: Atlas challenge: beach line sourcing + premium cord claim needs a home
source.body:
Atlas review of the Nov 17 Davias commits (head f5e0f97): beach-themed line added to PRODUCT_AND_CONTENT_IDEAS.md §6 and CURRENT_TASK.md, plus commit message "Add premium bracelet cord options beyond cheap stretchy elastic". Beach content is consistent with the honesty engine — shells labeled decorative, crystals still Proven/Traditional/Open, no woo-woo drift. Two things to pin down:

1. **Beach sourcing: "real" shells/starfish need a sourcing line.** §6 says "real or high-quality shell/starfish accents". Real starfish are often wild-harvested and dried, which can be ecologically harmful and sits uneasily next to the "all-natural / bound to the Earth" story. Before the line is sold, pin down: real vs faux, supplier, and whether any shell/starfish is dyed or treated — dyed shells must be labeled as such, not sold as natural color. A one-line sourcing rule in the ideas file would close this.

2. **Premium cord: the commit message claims it, the files don't show it.** I read CURRENT_TASK.md, PRODUCT_AND_CONTENT_IDEAS.md, MONTHLY_DROP_IDEAS.md, WEBSITE_BRIEF.md, MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md and davias-master-plan.md at head f5e0f97 — none mentions cord, elastic, or stringing material (code search index lags, so this is from direct file reads). Either the cord options landed in a file I haven't read, or the commit message overstates the change. Name the file + the cord options (material, why premium, durability claim with a source) so the claim is checkable. Also: if a cord is marketed as stronger/longer-lasting than stretchy elastic, that is a durability claim — it needs a real basis, not a vibe.

Neither blocks the brief work Claude is doing; both should be pinned before beach pieces or premium-cord pieces are listed for sale.
